 1          Plaintiffs W.A. Call Mfg. Co., Inc., a California corporation, Lisa Diaz d/b/a Legacy

 7   knowledge.
 8                                     NATURE OF THE ACTION
 9          1.      This is a putative class action lawsuit against Defendant for breach of contract and
10   unfair business practices, including the deliberate concealment of critical contract terms.
11          2.      Defendant has been and continues to engage in a systematic and pervasive scheme
12   to overbill its customers by surreptitiously increasing rates in amounts in excess of the agreed
13   upon contract rate, not providing notice of increases pursuant to Defendant’s contracts with its
14   customers, and increasing its customers’ rates more frequently than is permitted by the contracts.
15   Additionally, Defendant perpetrated an unlawful “automatic renewal” scheme to keep its
16   customers locked into contracts by concealing the automatic renewal terms from Plaintiffs.
17          3.      Defendant engaged in strong-arm tactics to force Plaintiffs into keeping their
18   service with Defendant by using threats of astronomical early termination fees calculated based
19   on the automatic renewal terms of which that Plaintiffs were never made aware.
20          4.      Defendant is a nationwide company that primarily provides fixed-wireless
21   Internet and telephony services to personal consumers, as well as to small business consumers.
22   According to Defendant’s website, “WiLine is present in 45 states and over 610 markets and
23   growing rapidly.”
24          5.      Defendant’s website asserts Defendant is operating in every state except Maine,
25   Nebraska, New Hampshire, South Dakota, and Wyoming, but is rapidly building out its service
26   areas in those remaining five states.
27          6.      In the Customer Service Agreement (“Service Agreement”) presented to its
28   customers, Defendant made no mention of increasing the service charge rates, automatic renewal

 1   of the contract, or a requirement to arbitrate disputes.
 2          7.      Instead, upon the signing of Defendant’s Service Agreement, a WiLine customer

 3   agrees to be bound “to this Order and Service Agreement Terms and Conditions as posted on
 4   www.wiline.com.”
 5          8.      This information is provided in the fine print using 8-point font in the Service
 6   Agreement.
 7          9.      The language is purposely ambiguous as it is written to imply the Service
 8   Agreement’s terms and conditions can be found at www.wiline.com.

28   with Defendant.
